newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Sweden questions how smoothly EMU pact will work.
newsitem.headline: Sweden questions how smoothly EMU pact will work.

text.p: Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson said a European Union pact to enforce fiscal discipline within monetary union was necessary, but questioned how well it would function.
Persson told reporters the pact was probably both important and necessary but added, "I'm not so totally certain that it will be able to function (effectively)."
The EU agreed the stability pact at its two-day summit in Dublin, due to end on Saturday night.

Persson did not elaborate on his doubts about how the pact would work, but pointed out difficult decisions lay ahead, including which countries are admitted to economic and monetary union (EMU), due to start in 1999.
He said he was very suspicious of all those who said that everything concerning EMU was now resolved. "I think we will see a few more crises ahead of us."
Separately, he told Reuters Financial Television that the stability pact was the summit's most important decision.
"Because without that, we would have lost momentum (in the drive towards EMU)," Persson said, adding he believed Sweden "can live with it" if it were to join EMU.
But he added, "You will have an ongoing discussion about EMU and the growth and stability pact...so what it will all look like in the end, I think it's too early to have an opinion."
